messages.author: MarcusVickEBC
messages.text: Across 16,000 simulations, AI confirms OFA has nothing to do with positioning in the slot for one timers.

messages.author: MarcusVickEBC
messages.text:
This game continues to amaze me. 

AI found a goal scoring set up that I wanted to test. 

I had it use Mike Modano, and do it the exact same way (same coordinates and pixels on the ice) 1000x against Roy and 1000x against Don Beaupre. 

610/1000 goals against Roy. 307/1000 goals against Beaupre.

messages.author: MarcusVickEBC
messages.text:
I just ran it again. 1000x again. 

620/1000 against Roy. 389/1000 against Beaupre.

messages.author: GaelicGopher
messages.text: Wonder how he’d do versus Darcy Wakaluk!!!!

messages.author: MarcusVickEBC
messages.text:
Goal percentage against both Roy and Beaupre for the scoring move in question. 

Something above using 5 SHP against Beaupre is causing the puck to go in far less. 

Each permutation of SHP and SHA was run 1000 times per goalie.

messages.author: MarcusVickEBC
messages.text:
So until you get to 5-5, 5-6, or 6-5…Beaupre is a far better goalie AGAINST THIS TYPE OF SCORING
MOVE than Roy.

messages.author: MarcusVickEBC
messages.text: Specifying “this type of scoring move” because I don’t want you to think this means Beaupre is a better goalie than Roy generally.

messages.author: MarcusVickEBC
messages.text: I’m running another 54,400 simulations now, changing tiny variables around the shot to see if any of them matter or change the save percentage.

messages.author: MarcusVickEBC
messages.text: 16 rating permutations, 17 different wind-up stop points, 100 attempts each, against both goalies.

messages.author: MarcusVickEBC
messages.text: The AI decides man. The AI decides.

messages.author: MarcusVickEBC
messages.text: And yea, apparently there are 17 different points where you can release your wind up on a shot.

messages.author: MarcusVickEBC
messages.text: The craziest thing is - the AI is playing the game. It’s not just simulating the code. It is showing me actual gameplay footage.

messages.author: MarcusVickEBC
messages.text: Most disappointing finding: sent it  Twitch clips of times where goalies go crazy and skate all the way up ice.  It has gone through the ROM and cannot figure out what causes that.

messages.author: MarcusVickEBC
messages.text:
Smolinski is the only player I found with this condition in your ROM’s default lineups. There is a concrete explanation.

Boston assigns him to both LW and the hidden extra-attacker slot. When you select him for C or RW, the replacement routine:

Finds his extra-attacker entry first.
Moves the displaced center/right winger into that entry.
Assigns Smolinski to your selected position—but leaves him at LW.
That creates the two visible Smolinski assignments.

I scanned all 28 teams × eight lineup records and executed 12,768 replacement tests using the original ROM routine. Only selecting Boston’s Smolinski at C or RW produced duplicate visible skaters from those stock records.

Simply trying another team’s extra attacker should not reproduce it: Smolinski uniquely starts with the necessary repeated entry. Ordinary replacements through this routine also cannot create that initial repetition for another player.
